name: F. H. Eaton
role: Pittsburgh man who summered at the Logging Camp, 1886
bio: F. H. Eaton of Pittsburgh arrived in March 1886 with Miss Hattie Eaton to spend the summer at the Logging Camp, and in June the paper quoted his delight at coming in from the Logging Camp soaked through by rain. In October 1886 he was called back to Pittsburgh by the serious illness of his son-in-law.

moments.label: Arrived from Pittsburgh to summer at the Logging Camp
Called home by his son-in-law's illness

mentions: Mr. and Mrs F. H. Eaton and Miss Hattie Eaton will arrive probably a week from to-night, to spend the summer in the Bad Lands.
Mr. and Mrs. F. H. Eaton, Miss Hattie, and Mr. Rook arrived from Pittsburgh last evening and this morning started for the Logging Camp where they will spend the summer.
F. H. Eaton brought the rain in with him yesterday from the Logging Camp. Although as wet as a drowned rat, the first thing he said was: "Ain't this glorious?"
Mr. F. H. Eaton was called suddenly to Pittsburgh, Tuesday morning, on account of the serious illness of his son-in-law.
Ralph Bagley of the Westinghouse air-brake company, and his wife and J. Cass Carpenter of the Pennsylvania railroad, arrived Saturday night and are visiting the Eatons.
